description: The configuration surface of the harbor chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

credentialsSecret.description: Name of the Secret holding every credential. Empty means "{release}-credentials".
credentialsSecret.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: docs/plan/12 § The pattern, once, piece 5. The platform MINTS these into the tenant's vault and writes the Secret; this chart only NAMES it. ⚠ It is deliberately not a value: goharbor/harbor-helm ships `harborAdminPassword: "Harbor12345"` as a live default while randomising every other credential in the same template, and a values key here would be one edit away from reproducing that.

imageRegistry.description: Where Harbor's seven images are pulled from.
imageRegistry.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: A platform escape hatch for an air-gapped mirror. Not a tenant setting: a registry whose own images come from somewhere the tenant chose is a supply chain the platform cannot vouch for.

enabled.description: Whether Harbor's core exports Prometheus metrics and a PodMonitor selects them. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". Turning it off removes the metrics port as well as the scrape, so nothing is left listening on an unscraped address.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

purgeProtection.description: Whether this registry may be destroyed before its seven-day recovery window is out. Once true it stays true for the rest of the registry's life, and a purge is refused while it is set — a flag whose holder can clear it and then purge is one round-trip of protection.

replicas.description: How many replicas of each stateless component — the API core, the web portal and the job service — run. Two is the smallest count that survives a node drain. The registry itself, the database and Redis each own a volume and run one replica whatever this says.

sizing.description: CPU and memory for the registry pod, either by preset or explicitly. The other five components are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. The registry uses the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

class.description: StorageClass name for the image volume. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Image storage, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks. ⚠ This is a filesystem volume rather than the tenant's object-storage bucket, which is what docs/plan/13 asks for and what the platform cannot yet give it — see the registry's own documentation.

version.description: Harbor minor version. The platform pins the patch, because Harbor publishes image tags per patch and a bare minor resolves to nothing. A minor leaving support is a portal notice and a 120-day window — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions.
